h1:
Pattaya & Naklua Seafood
10 Spots Locals Eat At
intro: Pattaya and seafood go hand in hand, especially over on the Naklua side, an old fishing village where the boats come in and the catch hits the restaurants almost the same day. We've picked 10 spots that Pattaya locals and regulars genuinely talk about, with each area, a rough price range, and the dishes you can order without second-guessing — from waterfront tables facing the sunset to the hidden market spots the locals keep to themselves.
chips: 💸 From light bills to all-out feasts

blocks.html: Before the ranking, we'll be straight with you: most of Pattaya's truly fresh seafood is on the Naklua side (just past North Pattaya), because that's the old fishing district. The Jomtien Beach side leans more on the long sandy-beach atmosphere. We've counted both, because Pattaya locals eat on both. The prices listed are rough per-head ranges based on a group coming together and splitting the bill. Seafood prices swing with the season and the size of the catch — long holidays mean crowds and things selling out fast, so give yourself extra time and call ahead to be safe.

blocks.text: 10 Pattaya & Naklua Seafood Spots Locals Eat At

items.name: Mum Aroi (Naklua Branch)
items.blurb: The name that comes up first when people talk about Pattaya seafood. It sits right on the Naklua waterfront with hundreds of tables, views of old fishing boats and the sunset, and live music in the evening. The catch is fresh and the prices are fair. Regular orders include phat ruea pohe (the house stir-fried mixed vegetables), grilled river prawns, the crab-roe chili dip, and a packed tom yum. It gets busy Saturday and Sunday, so call ahead to book a waterfront table.

items.name: Krua Laew Tae R-Rom
items.blurb: A Thai-and-seafood spot in the North Pattaya-Naklua area that earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand (the good-value pick). The cooking is bold and home-style, using local ingredients. It's not a big place and people love it, so book ahead during peak times. Better suited to those who want serious home cooking over a view.
items.meta: Phaniat Chang Rd, Naklua · in town · book ahead

items.name: Je Juk Seafood (Branch 3)
items.blurb: A well-known spot on the Sukhumvit-Pattaya side, with fresh catch and a nice atmosphere. Pattaya locals point to Branch 3 in particular. The dishes people mention are the deep-fried grouper with tamarind sauce, steamed crab, and baked prawns with glass noodles. Good for a family meal or a bigger group.
items.meta: Sukhumvit-Pattaya area · in town · open till late

items.name: Je Nong Seafood
items.blurb: A waterfront spot on the Naklua side near Saphan Yao (the long pier). The draw is the huge spread of fresh catch to choose from — it's like the sea has been brought to the front of the restaurant. You pick what you want live and have it cooked. Wide sea views, good for a long, relaxed evening.

items.name: Hoy Krang Luak & Krua Je Tum (Theprasit 17)
items.blurb: A hidden spot in the Theprasit area that locals pass along. Fresh catch daily, a good cook's touch, and prices that aren't steep compared with the waterfront places. No sea view, but you come for the flavor and value. Good for anyone wanting to dodge the tourist zone.
items.meta: Theprasit Soi 17 · in town · hidden spot

items.name: P. Pramong Seafood
items.blurb: The standout here is its own prawn and crab tanks on site, so freshness is pretty much guaranteed. It's in the North Pattaya area, with prawns and crab as the headliners. Good for anyone who puts freshness above everything else.

items.name: Non Seafood (behind Lan Pho Market)
items.blurb: A small, tucked-away spot behind Naklua's Lan Pho Market, with sea views from the second floor. Locals love the crab dishes. It's the kind of place regulars know about — nothing flashy, but the food is good. Parking is limited, so coming outside peak hours is easier.
items.meta: Behind Lan Pho Market, Naklua · waterfront · open 09:00–21:00

items.name: Krua Lung Chaew (Nong Mai Kaen)
items.blurb: A spot that made the 2025 Michelin Guide, known for its fried fish. The location is out past central Pattaya toward Nong Mai Kaen, so it suits anyone with a car who doesn't mind driving out a bit for serious home cooking. It gets busy on holidays.
items.meta: Nong Mai Kaen (out of town) · car needed

items.name: Sri Nuan Seafood (Jomtien front)
items.blurb: On the Jomtien Beach side — a wide place with plenty of tables and fresh catch. People particularly praise the seafood dipping sauce. Great for a big group or a family, and you get the long-beach atmosphere as a change from the Naklua side.

items.name: Ban Amphoe Seafood (Na Jomtien)
items.blurb: A beachfront spot in the Na Jomtien area with open sea views, fresh catch, and easy seating. Good for anyone staying around Jomtien-Na Jomtien who wants seafood with a sea view without driving all the way to Naklua.
items.meta: Na Jomtien · beachfront · open till late

blocks.title: How to read the prices
blocks.html: The per-head prices above assume a group ordering and sharing. If you order a big river prawn, a large mud crab, or lobster, the bill climbs fast, because these are charged by weight. When picking fresh catch, always ask the price per kilo and the weight first, so there's no surprise when the bill comes.

blocks.html: If you're not sure what to order, here are the dishes most Pattaya seafood spots do well and that people order often. Pick what fits your budget and group size.

items: Grilled river prawns / grilled prawns — the star of the table, dipped in seafood sauce. Charged by weight, so ask the price per kilo before ordering.
Steamed crab / crab in curry powder — fresh mud crab steamed for sweet meat, or stir-fried in curry powder with egg. Price depends on crab size.
Blanched cockles / oysters — a lighter way to start the meal, cheaper than the big mains, with a punchy dipping sauce.
Sea bass / grouper — steamed with lime, fried with fish sauce, or fried with tamarind sauce, however you like it.
Seafood tom yum / mixed seafood tom yum — sip it hot with prawns, squid and shellfish, spicy and sour and balanced. Easy to share around the whole table.
Crab-roe chili dip / phat ruea pohe — local dishes that many Naklua spots do well, eaten with fresh vegetables and steamed rice.

blocks.text: Naklua vs Jomtien — which side to pick

items.name: Naklua side
items.blurb: The old fishing district with the freshest catch. Legendary spots like Mum Aroi and the hidden ones around Lan Pho Market are here, with fishing-boat views and sunsets. Best for those who care about flavor and freshness.

items.name: Jomtien-Na Jomtien side
items.blurb: You get the long sandy-beach atmosphere, with wide places and plenty of tables. Good for a big group or if you're already staying around Jomtien, with relaxed beachfront seating for as long as you like.

blocks.title: Enjoy Pattaya with peace of mind
blocks.html: Pattaya has nightlife districts like Walking Street. If you're heading out after dinner, travel sensibly, keep an eye on your valuables and wallet, and don't leave your things with strangers. If you're planning to take a boat to Koh Larn the next morning, always check the weather and sea conditions first — the water on this coast changes fast in the rainy season.

blocks.text: Tips for eating Pattaya seafood well and worry-free

items: Book ahead on holidays — popular waterfront spots fill up fast, especially sunset-view tables. Booking ahead is the safe move.
Ask the price of fresh catch before ordering — prawns, crab and fish are charged by weight. Ask the price per kilo and have it weighed in front of you so the bill doesn't confuse you.
Go before sunset — if you want both the view and a parking spot, early evening beats arriving late. Some items sell out fast.
Plan for parking — some hidden market spots have limited parking. On a busy day, parking further away and walking can be easier.
Check that the catch is fresh — fresh prawns, shellfish and crab are firm and don't smell strongly fishy. If you're unsure, pick a place with its own tanks or one the locals go to regularly.

faq.q: Where in Pattaya is the freshest seafood?
faq.a: The Naklua side is Pattaya's old fishing district, and most of the catch comes ashore around there. Legendary spots like Mum Aroi and the hidden ones around Lan Pho Market are in this zone. If you're after fresh catch and a good cook's touch, Naklua is the side Pattaya locals think of first. Jomtien, meanwhile, stands out for its long-beach atmosphere.

faq.q: Roughly how much is a Pattaya seafood meal per person?
faq.a: If you come as a group and share, it averages around ฿300–600 per person at a typical place. But if you order a big river prawn, a large mud crab, or lobster, the bill goes up because these are charged by weight. We'd always recommend asking the price per kilo and having it weighed before you order.

faq.q: Are there any Michelin Pattaya seafood spots?
faq.a: Yes — for example, Krua Laew Tae R-Rom in the Naklua area earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand (the good-value pick), and Krua Lung Chaew made the 2025 Michelin Guide, known for its fried fish. Both lean on the cooking more than the view, so book ahead during peak times.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table at Pattaya seafood restaurants?
faq.a: On a quiet weekday you can usually walk in, but on Saturdays, Sundays and long holidays the popular waterfront spots fill up fast, especially the sunset-view tables. We'd recommend calling ahead, and at some hidden spots with limited parking, allow extra time to find a space.

faq.q: When is the best time to eat Pattaya seafood?
faq.a: Early evening before sunset is a good window — you get the view, a parking spot, and the catch is still fully stocked, since some items sell out fast on busy days. If you're planning a sea activity the next day, like a boat to Koh Larn, don't forget to check the weather and sea conditions first.
